$description: Tier 1 · core primitives · two faces shared by every brand (decided 2026-10-30): Archivo is the text face (headlines, body, labels, small print); Atkinson Hyperlegible Next is the data face (values a reader compares, checks or copies). The font.match values make the data face sit with the text face on one line; they were measured from the two font files and must be re-measured if either face changes.

sans.$description: Text face: headlines, body, labels, captions, legal small print. Google Fonts, SIL Open Font License; variable weight 100–900 and width 62–125.

data.$description: Data face: table values, device IDs, registration numbers, coordinates, times, specifications, prices. Chosen for unambiguous digits (open 4, slashed 0). Google Fonts, SIL Open Font License; weight 200–800 with italics. Always use with the font.match values.

mono.$description: PLACEHOLDER mono for code, coordinates and telemetry readouts.

match.$description: How the data face is matched to the text face. Measured 2026-10-30 from the Google Fonts files and verified in Chrome (AID workspace: docs/studies/type-evidence/). Re-measure if either face changes.

cap-height.$description: Use as font-size-adjust: cap-height <value> on data text. The data face's figures are as tall as its capitals, so this renders its digits at the text face's figure height (0.698 em) without changing font-size or line height.

design-scale.$description: For tools without font-size-adjust (Figma, Google Slides, Canva): set data text at this multiple of the text size beside it, e.g. 14 → 14.6, 16 → 16.7.

weight.$description: Data-face weight with the same stroke thickness as the text-face weight of the same name, after matching size.
